## Description

The Python 3 program reads the sizes of the mochi from standard input and prints the maximum number of kagamimochi that can be formed simultaneously. Each kagamimochi consists of two distinct mochi, with the top mochi at most half the size of the bottom mochi.

## Preconditions

- **PRE-1 (Unverified)** Standard input contains the integer \(N\) on the first line and exactly \(N\) integer sizes on the second line, with \(2 \le N \le 500{,}000\).
- **PRE-2 (Unverified)** Each size is between \(1\) and \(10^9\), inclusive. The sizes are in nondecreasing order, and repeated sizes are allowed.

## Postconditions

- **POST-1 (Unverified)** Standard output contains one integer \(K\), the maximum attainable number of simultaneous kagamimochi.
- **POST-2 (Unverified)** There are \(K\) disjoint pairs that satisfy the size rule. Each input position represents a separate mochi, even when sizes repeat, and each mochi can appear in at most one pair. A top mochi exactly half the size of its bottom mochi is allowed.
- **POST-3 (Unverified)** No set of \(K+1\) disjoint pairs satisfies the size rule. The output is between \(0\) and \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), inclusive, and is \(0\) exactly when no valid pair exists.

## Test suggestions

- Under PRE-1 and PRE-2, check that the two sizes \(2,4\) yield \(1\) and \(2,3\) yield \(0\) to exercise the size threshold (POST-1 through POST-3).
- Check that \(1,1,2,2,2\) yields \(2\) to exercise repeated sizes and an odd number of mochi (PRE-2, POST-2, POST-3).
- Check that \(1,2,3,5\) yields \(2\) to exercise maximum simultaneous pairing (POST-1 through POST-3).
- Check that 250,000 mochi of size \(1\) followed by 250,000 of size \(10^9\) yield \(250{,}000\) (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-3).

## Unspecified behavior

Behavior for input outside PRE-1 or PRE-2 is unspecified. When several pairings attain the maximum, the choice of pairing is unspecified.
